newsitem.title: USA: Hecla Mining sets Lucky Friday mine expansion.
newsitem.headline: Hecla Mining sets Lucky Friday mine expansion.

text.p: Hecla Mining Co's board of directors has approved expanding the Lucky Friday mine in Idaho in order to double silver production there.
The board also approved final mine design and engineering plans for the expansion area, called the Gold Hunter deposit.

The expanded area is about 5,000 feet northwest of the Lucky Friday vein currently being mined. The Gold Hunter deposit's main vein is nearly twice the silver grade and twice the width of the Lucky Friday vein, Hecla said in a statement.
It is expected to push the mine's annual silver production to over 4.0 million ounces by 1998 from 1.9 million in 1996.

About $16 million has been approved to fully develop the area over the next two years. Over the next 10-12 months, mining in the Lucky Friday vein will be scaled back in favor of production from the Gold Hunter expansion area.

Hecla said it will continue exploration to expand the Gold Hunter ore body. The potential resource is currently estimated at 50 million ounces or more of silver. Total proven and probable reserves at Lucky Friday, including the expansion area, are 18.5 million ounces of silver.
